_readme: Single source of truth for navigation, SEO metadata, the catalog, and the sitemap in the English site root. Human-readable fields are translation units tracked in i18n/ledger.json. Rebuild with: SITE_ROOT=en node scripts/build_nav.js

site.title: Home Assistant Onboarding Guide
site.subtitle: From setup to everyday use
site.description: A 22-chapter Home Assistant guide with 3 appendices, covering login, system settings, floors and areas, dashboards, notifications, automations, protocols, integrations, energy monitoring, history, voice assistants and LLMs, Docker architecture, and remote access. Each chapter takes about 10 minutes.
site.footerMeta: Screenshots show the official Home Assistant interface. Home Assistant is a trademark of the Open Home Foundation; this site is not affiliated with it.

hub._readme: index.html is the manually maintained hub for four resource types; build_nav does not modify it. build_nav generates the tutorial catalog at the file named by catalog. Each entry in pages is a self-contained handbook with its own head and styles, included in the sitemap and the check_links allowlist.

chapters.title: Log in to Home Assistant
chapters.card: Learn the login page, “Stay logged in,” and when to use the web interface or Companion App.
chapters.description: Learn three ways to find your Home Assistant URL, how Owner and Administrator accounts differ, when to use “Stay logged in,” and how the web interface compares with the Companion App.

chapters.title: System settings
chapters.card: Set the correct time zone, language, units, and location so that later automations run as expected.
chapters.description: Configure the Home Assistant time zone, language, unit system, and location so that time- and sun-based automations run correctly.

chapters.title: Floors and areas
chapters.card: Map your home’s floors and rooms so dashboards, voice control, and automations understand where devices are.
chapters.description: Create floors and areas in Home Assistant and assign devices to them, enabling natural controls such as “turn on the living-room lights.”

chapters.title: Naming and labels
chapters.card: Turn an opaque entity ID into a clear name, then use labels to group related devices and automations.
chapters.description: Plan clear Home Assistant names and entity IDs, and understand how labels and categories classify entities, devices, automations, and scripts.

chapters.title: User management
chapters.card: Create accounts for household members, tenants, and guests, with appropriate permissions for each person.
chapters.description: Understand the difference between users and persons, configure household and guest access, enable MFA, and calibrate mobile location tracking and zone radii.

chapters.title: Dashboards
chapters.card: Put frequently used lights, covers, and climate controls where everyone can find them.
chapters.description: Edit Home Assistant dashboards, add cards and views, choose among four view types, and build a layout that works for the whole household.

chapters.title: Notifications
chapters.card: Install the Companion App, connect a phone, and send your first push notification.
chapters.description: Install the Home Assistant Companion App, connect a phone, send a test notification, and create actionable notifications with buttons.

chapters.title: Your first automation
chapters.card: Use the trigger-condition-action model to turn on a light at sunset without falling into the device_id trap.
chapters.description: Build a “turn on the lights at sunset” automation, learn why entity_id is usually preferable to device_id, and understand run modes and Blueprints.

chapters.title: Backups
chapters.card: Configure automatic backups in three minutes so you can experiment and recover with confidence.
chapters.description: Create manual and scheduled Home Assistant backups, choose safe storage, and restore either a running installation or a replacement system.

chapters.title: Scripts
chapters.card: Package repeated actions into a reusable, parameterized script that dashboards, automations, and voice control can call.
chapters.description: Learn how scripts differ from automations, add fields, choose Single, Restart, Queued, or Parallel mode, and call scripts in four ways.

chapters.title: Device settings
chapters.card: Read the device page, update firmware, manage entities, download diagnostics, and use Repairs.
chapters.description: Understand the Home Assistant device page: rename devices and entities, disable or hide entities, update firmware, download diagnostics, and resolve Repairs.

chapters.title: Domain reference
chapters.card: A practical reference to common domains, their actions, dashboard cards, and frequent pitfalls.
chapters.description: Reference common actions, cards, and pitfalls for light, switch, climate, cover, media_player, lock, vacuum, fan, camera, sensor, and notify domains.

chapters.title: Themes and appearance
chapters.card: Choose light or dark mode, install a community theme, and tailor Home Assistant’s appearance for each user.
chapters.description: Configure light and dark modes, install community themes through HACS, apply themes per user or view, and customize theme variables and branding.

chapters.title: Integrations
chapters.card: Connect weather, music, location, calendar, and other external services to Home Assistant.
chapters.description: Follow the integration setup process, connect services such as weather, music, location, and calendars, compare local and cloud integrations, and diagnose or remove an integration.

chapters.title: Communication protocols
chapters.card: Compare Wi-Fi, Zigbee, Z-Wave, Matter, Thread, Bluetooth, KNX, Modbus, and MQTT before buying devices.
chapters.description: Compare major smart-home protocols, learn their hardware and integration requirements, and use a practical checklist before purchasing devices.

chapters.title: To-do lists and calendars
chapters.card: Move household reminders into shared to-do lists and calendars that can trigger automations.
chapters.description: Create local to-do lists and calendars, connect Google Calendar, add dashboard cards, and trigger automations from calendar events.

chapters.title: Energy dashboard and ESG practices
chapters.card: Turn energy readings into useful charts, cost tracking, baselines, and defensible reports.
chapters.description: Select suitable sensors, configure the Energy dashboard, integrate power into energy, track local tariffs and costs, and analyze efficiency improvements.

chapters.title: History, Recorder, and data export
chapters.card: Learn where Home Assistant stores history, how long it lasts, how to export it, and how to keep the database healthy.
chapters.description: Understand History, Logbook, Recorder retention, and long-term statistics; export CSV data and evaluate MariaDB, InfluxDB, and Grafana options.

chapters.title: Voice assistants and LLM integration
chapters.card: Build an Assist pipeline, then compare local and cloud speech and LLM options with their privacy and cost trade-offs.
chapters.description: Configure Assist, wake words, speech-to-text and text-to-speech, connect an LLM conversation agent, and compare local and cloud options for privacy and cost.

chapters.title: Add-ons and Docker architecture
chapters.card: Understand how Supervisor-managed Docker containers power add-ons and how to troubleshoot them.
chapters.description: Compare Home Assistant installation types, understand Supervisor and Docker concepts, install useful add-ons, read logs, and automate off-device backups.

chapters.title: Networking and remote access
chapters.card: Set a stable local address and compare four secure ways to reach Home Assistant away from home.
chapters.description: Configure a DHCP reservation and compare Nabu Casa, Cloudflare Tunnel, VPN, and DDNS with a reverse proxy, including trusted proxies and security rules.

chapters.title: Life logging and custom dashboards
chapters.card: Track habits, household spending, maintenance, and notes, then turn those records into useful dashboards.
chapters.description: Use Home Assistant helpers for habit tracking, household spending, maintenance reminders, and messages, then visualize the data with charts and Sections views.

appendices.navLabel: A · HACS, add-ons, and remote access
appendices.title: Ecosystem: HACS, add-ons, and remote access
appendices.pagerTitle: A · HACS, add-ons, and remote access
appendices.card: Compare official add-ons, the HACS community store, and four remote-access options.
appendices.description: Explore the official add-on store, Home Assistant Community Store (HACS), and the trade-offs among Nabu Casa, DDNS, VPN, and Cloudflare Tunnel.

appendices.title: Scenes, helpers, and groups
appendices.card: Use scenes, ten helper types, and groups as reusable building blocks for automations.
appendices.description: Learn how scenes, 10 types of helper, and groups work together as reusable building blocks for smart-home logic.

appendices.title: Before installation: hardware and HAOS
appendices.card: No host yet? Choose hardware and storage, install HAOS, and complete first-time setup.
appendices.description: Compare HAOS, Supervised, Container, and Core; choose a Raspberry Pi or mini PC and suitable storage; flash the image and complete first boot.
